newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - down at least 1/2 point.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - down at least 1/2 point.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices sank at least 1/2 and as much as 3/4 point in morning trading, following a stronger-than expected jobs report for December.

The damage is not yet as bad as in the Treasury market, where yields rose to three-month highs. Fears that strong job growth will lead to a Fed tightening helped push the long bond 1-22/32 lower at 95-2/32 to a 6.89 percent yield.
The Labor Department said the U.S. economy created 262,000 jobs last month, compared to expectations among economists for a 192,000 gain.
The muni market typically lags Treasury swings, and muni traders said it is likely to catch up to the gains over the next few sessions.

In light secondary market activity, yields on Florida Board of Education 5-1/2s of 2026 were five basis points higher at 5.78 percent. Sikeston, Mo., MBIA 5.0s of 2022 were up six basis points to 5.77 percent.

Debt futures were also sharply lower. The March municipal contract was down 1-6/32 to 113-29/32 and March T-bonds fell 1-14/32 to 109-31/32. The MOB spread widened to 126 ticks from 118 at the close on Thursday.
